label: prf:skein-generation
title: Proof of Skein generation
html:
Proof. Proof of Skein generation

Generators. A knot type K is fundamental if its hyperbolic volume vanishes: \mathrm{Vol}(K) = 0. By the geometrization of knot complements, these are precisely the torus knots (and the unknot). In the particle dictionary, the fundamental knots are the fermions: the unknot (neutrino), trefoil 3_1 (electron), cinquefoil 5_1 (tau), and the torus(p,2) family.

Generation. The Skein module \mathrm{Sk}_q is generated as an algebra by the fundamental knot types \{K_i\}_{i \in \mathcal{F}} and the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}. Every hadron H \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}} admits a terminal Skein resolution: iterating the Skein relation

  q \cdot L_+ -  q^{-1} \cdot L_-
  =  (q - q^{-1}) \cdot L_0

at every crossing terminates in a finite polynomial

  [H] =  \sum_{\alpha} c_\alpha(q) \cdot
  [K_{i_1}] \cdots [K_{i_k}]

where each [K_{i_j}] is the class of a fundamental knot and c_\alpha(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}].

Mass from linking. By (Skein-resolution mass formula), \mathfrak{m}(H) = Q(q) \cdot \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) + \sum_i \mathrm{Vol}(K_i)/\hbar_q^2. For hadrons composed entirely of fundamental (torus-knot) constituents, \mathrm{Vol}(K_i) = 0 for all i, so the entire inertial mass arises from the linking topology, \mathfrak{m}(H) = Q(q) \cdot \mathfrak{m}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}). \square
